newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh faces higher trade imbalance -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh faces higher trade imbalance -- paper.

text.p: Bangladesh faces a deteriorating balance of trade with its Asian neighbours, The Financial Express newspaper said on Wednesday.
Bangladesh's imports from 20 Asian trading partners totalled $3.21 billion in fiscal 1994/95 (July-June), up $975 million from the previous year, the paper said quoting government officials.
The country's exports to these countries rose to $466.24 million in the year from $318.90 million in 1993/94, the paper added.
It did not give 1995/96 figures but said the trend was similar to the previous year.
China, Hong Kong, India, Japan and South Korea are among Bangladesh's leading trading partners.
Imports from China surged to $420 million in 1994/95 from $223.16 million compared with exports of $45.29 million in 1994/95 and $13.22 million the previous year.

Imports from India, Bangladesh's biggest trading partner, amounted to $688.54 million in 1994/95, up by $275 million from the previous year. Exports also rose but stood at a meagre $45.17 million in 1994/95 and $16.81 million a year earlier.
